page.layout: One column of running text, set in the centre of the page. Running head above the text. The catchword sits at the right below the last line. No marginal notes; a brace at the right beside "falsum" groups lines of text and is not a note.

main_text.p: ille nuncius alterius & interpres, Παυλ[?]ος ὁ ἡγούμεν[?]ος τῷ λόγῳ[?], Actor. xiv. 11, Atque ita Paulus Mercurius, Barnabas Jupiter, & hinc nascitur conclusio Cameronianæ oppositæ. Fuisse Paulum præ Barnaba, ea in dicendo majestate, eo eloquio, quod sublimitas illa styli maxime decere videatur.

XIV. Addit tandem, Barnabam videri paulò incitatiorem fuisse animo, quam Paulum. Hoc autem unde? Quia hinc natus ille paroxysmus, qui narratur Act. xv. 39. Quid si liberalius demus omnia Cameroni, eone conficietur Epistolam Barnabæ adscribi debere? Quia forte Barnabas ad iram & contentionem pronior? Quid commune hic, cum gravi illa Epistolæ, partim masculè docentis, partim suavissimè solantis & erigentis, majestate? Sed antecedens, quantum quidem ex Sacris assequimur, videtur esse falsum. Pauli animus ille concitatior, ubiq; conspicuus. Sic Petro in os resistit, Ananiam acriùs increpat, Corinthios, Galatas, vehementer redarguit. Pauli acta omnia,

page.notes: The Greek in the first line is partly worn and its accents and letters are uncertain; the readings marked [?] are the likely letters. The page number is faint at the top left. The catchword "dicta," is the word that opens the next page. The Greek and the reference "Actor. xiv. 11," follow the printed order.
